en: The Philippine archipelago consists of exactly 7,641 islands, grouped into three main geographical divisions: Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao.
Standing at 2,954 meters above sea level, Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest peak in the Philippines.
Taal Volcano is one of the smallest active volcanoes in the world, located entirely within a lake called Taal Lake.
The Cagayan River in northern Luzon is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers to the Pacific Ocean.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a massive surface area of about 911 square kilometers.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features an 8.2-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the West Philippine Sea.
Mount Mayon in Albay is famous for its nearly perfect conical shape and has erupted over 50 times in recorded history.
The island of Luzon is the largest in the Philippines, covering about 109,965 square kilometers, making it larger than South Korea.
Maria Cristina Falls in Iligan City drops 124 meters, providing significant hydroelectric power to the industrial centers of northern Mindanao.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park covers 96,828 hectares and protects over 600 species of fish and 360 species of coral.
Baguio City receives an average of over 4,000 millimeters of rainfall annually, making it one of the wettest cities in the country.
The Philippine Trench reaches a maximum depth of 10,540 meters, making it the deepest oceanic trench in the Philippine Sea.
